PROJECT: Asynchronous-AER Spike Router (4-phase REQ/ACK, 16-entry routing table, GF180)
PROJECT_DETAILS: GF180mcuD synchronous implementation of a 4-input / 4-output AER (address-event-representation) spike router. Time-multiplexed AER input and output buses each carry one event at a time as a 2-bit channel tag plus 6-bit address. Each incoming event is captured using a double-flop-synchronised 4-phase bundled-data REQ/ACK handshake, looked up in a 16-entry {dst_ch, dst_addr} routing table (or bypassed to pass through unchanged), queued in a 4-deep FIFO, and emitted out the output port with another 4-phase REQ/ACK handshake. Drops on FIFO overflow are counted in a 16-bit saturating drop counter with a sticky overflow_ever bit. Per-input 8-bit saturating event counters and IN_LAST / OUT_LAST debug latches are readable over SPI. 25 MHz signoff clock.
AUTHOR: Prof. Santhosh Sivasubramani, IIT Delhi

PROJECT: Neuromorphic PUF (distinct-tap LFSR arbiter + memristor XOR, GF180)
PROJECT_DETAILS: GF180mcuD digital Physical Unclonable Function: 8 distinct-tap maximal-length 10-bit LFSRs act as synthesizable virtual ring-oscillators, a 6-bit challenge selects a pair, and an arbiter FSM compares their popcounts over a programmable 2^N-cycle window (N in 4..12) to produce a response bit. 64 challenges accumulate into a 64-bit response that can be XORed with a host-loaded memristor vector for dual-entropy mode.
